literal: He was buried at the Xingsheng Buddhist Temple.
idiomatic: He was buried at Xingsheng Temple.

literal: After more than four hundred days a great interment was finally performed; his complexion and hair were all as if alive. Popular lore says those born on the fifth day of the fifth month do not suffer decay of the brain.
idiomatic: More than four hundred days passed before he received full burial; his complexion and hair looked as if he were still alive. Folk wisdom holds that those born on the fifth day of the fifth month never rot above the neck.

literal: Chuo's brothers all called their father elder brother, their principal mother mother dear, their wet nurse elder sister, and their wives little sister.
idiomatic: Among Chuo's brothers, all called their father "Elder Brother," the principal mother "Mother Dear," the wet nurse "Elder Sister," and their wives "Little Sister."

literal: When Qi perished, his consort Lady Zheng, whom Emperor Wu of Zhou favored, requested burial for Chuo.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, his consort Lady Zheng — a favorite of Emperor Wu of Zhou — petitioned for Chuo's burial.

literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to bury him north of Yongping Tomb.
idiomatic: An edict ordered him buried north of Yongping Tomb.

literal: Prince Yan of Langya, courtesy name Renwei, was Wucheng's third son.
idiomatic: Prince Yan of Langya, courtesy name Renwei, was Gao Zhan's third son.

literal: Initially enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, he was appointed opening-establishment grand master, attendant within the palace, supervisor of the Secretariat, metropolitan governor of the capital region, grand general commanding the imperial guard, and concurrently imperial censor-in-chief; he was transferred to minister over the masses, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, grand general, recorder of affairs of the Masters of Writing, and grand marshal.
idiomatic: Initially enfeoffed Prince of Dongping, he received posts as opening-establishment grand master, palace attendant, Secretariat supervisor, metropolitan governor of the capital region, commander of the imperial guard and concurrent imperial censor-in-chief; later he rose to minister over the masses, chief minister of the Masters of Writing, grand general, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and grand marshal.

literal: Under the old Wei system, when the censor-in-chief went out the route was cleared; he and the crown prince traveled by separate roads. Princes and nobles all halted their carriages at a distance, removed their oxen, set the yokes on the ground, and waited for the censor to pass; if anyone was tardy or disobedient, red clubs struck him.
idiomatic: Under the old Wei rule, when the censor-in-chief went abroad the road was cleared and he and the crown prince used separate routes. Princes and nobles all stopped their carriages at a distance, unhitched the oxen, laid the yokes on the ground, and waited for the censor to pass; tardiness or disobedience brought blows from red clubs.

literal: After the capital moved to Ye this ceremony had gradually died out; Wucheng, wishing to magnify Yan's favor, had it restored in full according to the old statute.
idiomatic: After the capital moved to Ye this ceremony had faded; Gao Zhan, wanting to exalt Yan's position, restored it entirely to the old form.

literal: The first time he left the Northern Palace to assume his duties as censor-in-chief, all the infantry and cavalry of the capital region, the staff of the army commander, the censor's full retinue, and the minister's ceremonial guard were completely provided.
idiomatic: The first time he left the Northern Palace to take up the censorate, the capital infantry and cavalry, the commander's entire staff, the censor's full retinue, and the minister's ceremonial escort were all deployed without exception.

literal: The emperor and Empress Hu spread a canopy outside the east gate of Hualin Garden and watched from behind a green gauze screen.
idiomatic: The emperor and Empress Hu set a pavilion outside the east gate of Hualin Garden and watched from behind a green gauze screen.

literal: He sent a palace eunuch galloping to the guard formation; entry was refused. Declaring he came by imperial order, red clubs instantly smashed his saddle; the horse bolted and the man fell.
idiomatic: He sent a palace eunuch galloping toward the guard line; they would not admit him. Claiming an imperial order, he was answered by red clubs that smashed his saddle — the horse bolted and he fell.

literal: The emperor laughed greatly and approved.
idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and approved.

literal: He issued another order to halt the carriage and converse at length; spectators filled the capital.
idiomatic: Another order kept the carriage halted while messages passed back and forth at length; onlookers filled the capital.

literal: Yan constantly remained in the palace, holding court from Han'guang Hall; all his uncles bowed to him.
idiomatic: Yan lived constantly in the palace, conducting affairs from Han'guang Hall; all his uncles bowed to him.

literal: When the emperor visited Bing Province, Yan usually stayed behind as regent; each time he escorted the imperial procession, he would turn back halfway or only after reaching Jinyang.
idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Bing Province, Yan usually remained as regent; each farewell escort ended halfway, or only after Jinyang.

literal: Wang Shiluo often accompanied the imperial train and arrived late; Wucheng wished to punish him. He pleaded, "Your servant parted from the Third Son and lingered without noticing how late it had grown.
idiomatic: Wang Shiluo often rode with the imperial train and once arrived late; Gao Zhan meant to punish him. He pleaded, "Your servant took leave of the Third Son and lingered without noticing how late it had grown.

literal: " Wucheng thought of Yan and wept; he pardoned Shiluo without inquiry.
idiomatic: " Gao Zhan thought of Yan and wept; he pardoned Shiluo without further inquiry.

literal: Yan's vessels, robes, toys, and ornaments all matched the Last Emperor's; everything he wanted was supplied by official requisition.
idiomatic: Yan's vessels, robes, ornaments, and playthings all matched Houzhu's; whatever he wanted the court supplied.

literal: Once at the Southern Palace he saw early plums chilled with ice. Returning, he cried in anger, "Elder Brother already has them — why should I go without!
idiomatic: Once at the Southern Palace he saw ice-chilled early plums. Returning, he raged: "Elder Brother already has them — why should I have none!

literal: " From then on Houzhu always received novelties first; any attendant or craftsman who failed to understand this was punished.
idiomatic: " After that Houzhu always received novelties first; any attendant or craftsman who missed the point was punished.

literal: Even the Retired Emperor and Empress Hu considered this insufficient.
idiomatic: Even the retired emperor and Empress Hu thought this still not enough.

literal: Yan often suffered sore throat; when the physician needled him, he kept his eyes open without blinking.
idiomatic: Yan often had a sore throat; when a physician needled him he never blinked.

literal: He also told the emperor, "Elder Brother is timid — how could he command those around him?
idiomatic: He told the emperor, "Elder Brother is soft — how could he command those around him?

literal: " The emperor always praised him: "This clever boy will surely achieve something.
idiomatic: " The emperor always said, "This sharp boy will amount to something.

literal: " Holding Houzhu inferior, he had thoughts of deposing him.
idiomatic: " Thinking Houzhu inferior, he entertained thoughts of deposing him.

literal: After Wucheng died, Yan's title was changed to Langya.
idiomatic: After Gao Zhan died, Yan's title was changed to Langya.

literal: Yan resented He Shikai, Luotipo, and the rest for their extravagant indulgence and grand house-building, and once said to them, "The houses you are building must be finished soon — why so slow?
idiomatic: Yan resented He Shikai, Luotipo, and the rest for their extravagance and grand house-building. Once he said, "The mansions you are raising will be finished soon enough — why so slow?

literal: " The two said to each other, "The Prince of Langya's eyes blaze — even at a few paces they pierce a man. Just now facing him briefly, we broke into a sweat without noticing; before the Son of Heaven in audience it is not even so.
idiomatic: " The two said to each other, "Prince Yan's eyes blaze — at a few paces they bore into you. That brief meeting left us sweating before we knew it; even before the emperor in audience it is not so.

literal: " From this they came to fear him.
idiomatic: " From this they came to fear him.

literal: In the second year of Wuping he was sent to live in the Northern Palace; he attended court toward the empress dowager only once every five days and no longer saw her daily.
idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he was moved to the Northern Palace; he attended court toward the empress dowager only once every five days and no longer saw her daily.

literal: In the fourth month an edict removed him as grand preceptor while all other offices were stripped; he retained only the censorate and oversight of the capital region.
idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict removed him as grand preceptor and stripped every other office; he kept only the censorate and oversight of the capital region.

literal: Since the northern city held an armory, they wished to move Yan outside before stripping him of military authority.
idiomatic: Because the northern city held the armory, they intended to move Yan outside first, then seize his military authority.

literal: Supervising secretary Wang Ziyi and Yan's attendants, opening-establishment officer Gao Shelou and palace attendant Liu Biqiang, urged Yan: "Your Highness has been pushed aside precisely because Shikai sowed discord — how can you leave the Northern Palace and enter the common throng?
idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Ziyi and Yan's attendants Gao Shelou and Liu Biqiang urged him: "You have been sidelined because Shikai stirred up trouble — how can you leave the Northern Palace and walk among common people?

literal: " Yan told attendant Feng Zicong, "Shikai's crimes are grave — I wish to kill him.
idiomatic: " Yan told attendant Feng Zicong, "Shikai's crimes are grave — I mean to kill him.

literal: " Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and enthrone Yan, and so encouraged the plan.
idiomatic: " Zicong inwardly wanted to depose the emperor and enthrone Yan, and egged him on.

literal: Yan then had Ziyi submit an impeachment of Shikai's crimes, requesting detention and interrogation.
idiomatic: Yan had Ziyi submit an impeachment of Shikai's crimes, asking that he be taken into custody and investigated.

literal: Zicong mixed other documents into the memorial; the Last Emperor did not examine it closely and approved.
idiomatic: Zicong mixed other papers into the memorial; Houzhu did not read closely and approved.

literal: Yan deceived army commander Kudi Fulian, saying, "By imperial order you are to seize Shikai.
idiomatic: Yan deceived army commander Kudi Fulian: "By imperial order, take Shikai.

literal: " Fulian consulted Zicong and asked to confirm the order with another memorial.
idiomatic: " Fulian consulted Zicong and asked to confirm the order by memorial.

literal: Zicong said, "The Prince of Langya bears the order — what need to memorialize again?
idiomatic: Zicong said, "Prince Yan already holds the order — why memorialize again?

literal: " Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized Shikai and delivered him to the censorate.
idiomatic: " Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized Shikai and sent him to the censorate.

literal: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the office and had Shikai beheaded on the spot.
idiomatic: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the censorate and had Shikai beheaded there.

literal: Yan's followers had intended only to kill Shikai; once that was done they pressed Yan: "The deed is done — there can be no turning back.
idiomatic: Yan's men had meant only to kill Shikai; once it was done they pressed him: "The thing is started — it cannot stop now.

literal: " Yan then led more than three thousand capital-region soldiers and encamped at Qianqiu Gate.
idiomatic: " Yan then led more than three thousand capital soldiers and encamped at Qianqiu Gate.

literal: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace troops to summon Yan.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace troops to summon Yan.

literal: Taozhi bowed from afar; Yan ordered him bound hand and foot for execution; the palace troops scattered.
idiomatic: Taozhi bowed from a distance; Yan ordered him bound for beheading; the palace troops fled.

literal: The emperor sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan. Yan refused, saying, "Shikai deserved ten thousand deaths — he plotted to depose His Majesty, shave Mother Dear's head and make her a nun, and therefore amassed troops to seize Sun Fengzhen's house; for this Your Servant falsified an order and executed him.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Feng Zicong again. Yan refused: "Shikai deserved death many times over — he plotted to depose the emperor, shave Mother Dear's head and make her a nun, and amassed troops to seize Sun Fengzhen's mansion; I falsified an order and killed him for that.

literal: If Elder Brother wishes to kill me I will not flee guilt; if he spares me, send Elder Sister to fetch me and I will enter at once.
idiomatic: If Elder Brother wishes to kill me I will not flee my guilt; if he spares me, let Elder Sister come fetch me and I will enter at once.

literal: " Elder Sister was Lu Lingxuan; Yan intended to lure her out and kill her.
idiomatic: " "Elder Sister" was Lu Lingxuan — Yan meant to lure her out and kill her.

literal: Lingxuan stood behind the emperor with a knife in hand; hearing this, she trembled.
idiomatic: Lingxuan stood behind the emperor with a knife; hearing this, she trembled.

literal: Han Changluan was sent to summon Yan again. As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe and remonstrated: "Unless you cut down the Tipo mother and son, Your Highness has no way inside.
idiomatic: Han Changluan was sent again. As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe: "Unless you kill Tipo and his mother, Your Highness cannot get in.

literal: " Princes Guangning and Ande had just come from the west and wished to help the cause. They said, "Why not go in?
idiomatic: " Princes Guangning and Ande had just arrived from the west and wanted to help. They said, "Why not go in?

literal: " Biqiang said, "Our numbers are too few.
idiomatic: " Biqiang said, "We are too few.

literal: " Prince Ande looked at the crowd and said, "When Emperor Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan it took only eighty men — now there are thousands; why say too few?
idiomatic: " Prince Ande looked at the host and said, "When Emperor Gao Yan killed Yang Zunyan it took only eighty men — now we are thousands; how can we be too few?

literal: " The Last Emperor wept and told the empress dowager, "If fate allows I may see Mother Dear again; if not, this is eternal parting.
idiomatic: " Houzhu wept to the empress dowager: "If fate allows I may see Mother Dear again; if not, this is farewell forever.

literal: " They hastily summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him too.
idiomatic: " They hastily summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.

literal: Guang heard Shikai had been killed, clapped his hands and laughed: "A dragon's son does business — naturally not like ordinary men.
idiomatic: Guang heard Shikai was dead, clapped his hands and laughed: "A dragon's son at work — of course not like ordinary men.

literal: " He entered to see the emperor in Yong Lane.
idiomatic: " He entered and saw the emperor in Yong Lane.

literal: The emperor led four hundred palace guards on foot and horseback, armed for battle, preparing to sortie.
idiomatic: The emperor led four hundred palace guards, armed for battle, preparing to sortie.

literal: Guang said, "These little fellows playing with weapons — grapple with them and all turns to chaos.
idiomatic: Guang said, "Boys playing soldier — clash with them and everything turns to chaos.

literal: A vulgar proverb runs, 'When a slave sees the master his heart dies.' Your Majesty should go to Qianqiu Gate yourself; Langya will surely not stir.
idiomatic: As the proverb says, 'When a slave sees the master his heart dies.' Your Majesty should go to Qianqiu Gate yourself; Langya dare not move.

literal: " Pi Jinghe also agreed; the Last Emperor followed their advice.
idiomatic: " Pi Jinghe agreed; Houzhu took their counsel.

literal: Guang walked ahead and had a man call out, "The master comes.
idiomatic: Guang walked ahead and had a man shout, "The master comes.

literal: " Yan's followers panicked and scattered.
idiomatic: " Yan's followers panicked and scattered.

literal: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called from afar; Yan still stood without advancing.
idiomatic: The emperor halted on the bridge and shouted from afar; Yan still would not move.

literal: Guang went to him and said, "The emperor's brother killed one Han — what hardship is that?
idiomatic: Guang went to him: "The emperor's brother killed one Han — what's the hardship in that?

literal: " He seized Yan's hand and forcibly pulled him forward.
idiomatic: " He seized Yan's hand and dragged him forward.

literal: He pleaded with the emperor: "The Prince of Langya is young — fat of belly and full of brains, he acts rashly; when he grows he will not again. I beg his crime be pardoned.
idiomatic: He pleaded with the emperor: "Prince Yan is young — thick-waisted and rash; grown, he will not act so again. I beg you pardon him.

literal: " The emperor snatched Yan's sword-ring and beat his braided hair with it at random; only after a long while did he release him.
idiomatic: " The emperor snatched Yan's sword-ring and beat his braided hair with it for a long while before letting him go.

literal: Fulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and commander Zhai Xiankui were seized in the rear garden; the emperor shot them personally and then had them beheaded, all dismembered and exposed beneath the capital's street.
idiomatic: Fulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and commander Zhai Xiankui were seized in the rear garden; the emperor shot them himself, then had them beheaded, dismembered, and exposed in the capital streets.

literal: The civil and military officers all wanted them killed.
idiomatic: Civil and military officers all wanted them killed.

literal: Guang said that since all were sons of meritorious nobles, fearing unrest among hearts, Zhao Yanshen also cited the Spring and Autumn Annals that blame falls on the commander — and so punishments were graded accordingly.
idiomatic: Guang said they were all sons of meritorious houses and feared unrest; Zhao Yanshen also cited the Spring and Autumn principle that blame falls on the commander — and sentences were graded accordingly.

literal: Before Yan yet fell under guilt, north of Ye there was a white-horse pagoda built by Shi Jilong for Master Cheng; Yan was about to repair it.
idiomatic: Before Yan was punished, north of Ye stood a white-horse pagoda that Shi Jilong had built for Master Cheng; Yan meant to restore it.

literal: A shaman said, "If this stupa is moved, the northern city will lose its lord.
idiomatic: A shaman said, "Move this stupa and the northern city loses its master.

literal: " He did not listen; breaking through to the second tier they found a white serpent several zhang long, which coiled away and vanished; within ten-odd days came defeat.
idiomatic: " He ignored the warning; breaking through to the second tier they found a white serpent several zhang long that coiled away and vanished — within ten-odd days came defeat.

literal: From then the empress dowager kept Yan within the palace and always tasted his food herself.
idiomatic: From then the empress dowager kept Yan in the palace and tasted every meal herself.

literal: Lu Lingxuan said to the emperor, "People call the Prince of Langya clever and bold, unmatched today; judging his countenance, he scarcely seems fit to be a subject.
idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan told the emperor, "People say Prince Yan is clever and bold, a match for no one today; his face scarcely looks like a subject's.

literal: Since the unauthorized killing he has lived in constant fear; one should plan early.
idiomatic: Since the killing he has lived in fear — better plan early.

literal: " He Hongzhen, who was always on good terms with He Shikai, also asked that Yan be killed.
idiomatic: " He Hongzhen, always close to He Shikai, also urged Yan's death.

literal: Undecided, they secretly sent a food carriage to fetch Zu Ting and ask him; Ting cited the Duke of Zhou's execution of Guan Shu and Ji You's poisoning of Qing Fu; the emperor accepted his words.
idiomatic: Still undecided, they secretly sent a food carriage for Zu Ting; he cited the Duke of Zhou executing Guan Shu and Ji You poisoning Duke Qing's killer; the emperor accepted this.

literal: When Yan was sent to Jinyang, Right Guard grand general Zhao Yuankan was made to lure and seize him.
idiomatic: When Yan was sent to Jinyang, right guard grand general Zhao Yuankan was told to lure and seize him.

literal: Yuankan said, "Your servant once served the late emperor and daily saw how he loved the prince; now I would rather die than do this.
idiomatic: Yuankan said, "I once served the late emperor and saw daily how he loved this prince; I would rather die than do this now.

literal: " The emperor sent Yuankan out as governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: " The emperor sent Yuankan away as governor of Ying Province.

literal: In the last ten days of the ninth month the emperor told the empress dowager, "Tomorrow I wish to hunt with Renwei, leaving early and returning early.
idiomatic: In the last ten days of the ninth month the emperor told the empress dowager, "Tomorrow I hunt with Renwei — out early, back early.

literal: " That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.
idiomatic: " That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.

literal: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder Brother calls — why will you not go?
idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder Brother calls — why won't you go?

literal: " Yan went out to Yong Lane; Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind him.
idiomatic: " Yan went out to Yong Lane; Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.

literal: Yan cried out, "I beg to see Mother Dear and Elder Brother!
idiomatic: Yan cried, "Let me see Mother Dear and Elder Brother!

literal: " Taozhi stuffed his mouth with his sleeve, hooded his head in the reversed robe, and carried him out; at Daming Palace his nose bled over his face and he was immediately killed — aged fourteen.
idiomatic: " Taozhi stuffed his mouth with his sleeve, covered his head in the reversed robe, and carried him out; at Daming Palace blood streamed from his nose across his face and he was killed at once — he was fourteen.

literal: He was not stripped of his boots; wrapped in a mat he was buried indoors.
idiomatic: His boots were never removed; wrapped in a mat, he was buried inside the palace.

literal: The emperor had someone notify the empress dowager; she wailed a dozen times and was immediately ushered into the hall.
idiomatic: The emperor sent word to the empress dowager; she wailed only a dozen cries before they hustled her into the hall.

literal: In the third month of the following year he was buried west of Ye; posthumously honored as Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to console the empress dowager.
idiomatic: The following third month he was buried west of Ye; posthumously he was titled Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to comfort the empress dowager.

literal: There were four posthumous sons; after a few months all were secretly killed.
idiomatic: Four posthumous sons were born; within months all were secretly killed.

literal: Prince Yan of Pingyang's grandson Shijun was made heir.
idiomatic: Shijun, grandson of Prince Yan of Pingyang, was made heir.

literal: Yan's consort was the daughter of Li Zuqin; she was advanced to empress of the Emperor of Chu and resided in Xuanze Palace.
idiomatic: Yan's consort was Li Zuqin's daughter; she was raised to empress of the Emperor of Chu and lived in Xuanze Palace.

literal: When Qi fell she remarried.
idiomatic: When Qi fell she remarried.

literal: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, courtesy name Renhong, was Wucheng's fourth son.
idiomatic: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, courtesy name Renhong, was Gao Zhan's fourth son.

literal: By nature a worthy elder, he had no misdeeds.
idiomatic: By nature he was a man of worth; he had no misdeeds.

literal: He held the rank of special advance, opening-establishment grand master, honorary-equal thirds grand master, and governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He held special advance, opening-establishment, honorary-equal thirds grand master, and the governorship of Ding Province.
